claims.who: Kōichirō Miyamoto of Musa-Shiya the Shirtmaker
claims.quote: According to some sources, the origin of aloha shirts can be traced to the 1920s or the early 1930s, when the Honolulu-based dry goods store "Musa-Shiya the Shirtmaker" under the proprietorship of Kōichirō Miyamoto, started making shirts out of colorful Japanese prints (especially kasuri).
claims.note: store made shirts from Japanese prints

claims.quote: It has also been contended that the aloha shirt was devised in the early 1930s by Chinese merchant Ellery Chun of "King-Smith Clothiers and Dry Goods", a store in Waikiki.
claims.note: Chun said to have devised it
